slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Not covered here? Ask us directly — same working day response.

slots.label: Question 1
slots.default: Do we still need strong passwords if we use MFA?

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Yes. Multi-factor authentication is an excellent additional layer, but it works best alongside strong, unique passwords. Together they make accounts far harder to compromise, which is why we combine secure password management with MFA rather than relying on either alone.

slots.label: Question 2
slots.default: What is a password manager and is it safe?

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: A password manager securely stores and generates complex, unique passwords so employees don’t have to remember or reuse them. Reputable business password managers encrypt credentials so only the user can access them, which is far safer than spreadsheets, documents or memorised passwords reused across systems.

slots.label: Question 3
slots.default: How do you handle shared accounts?

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Shared accounts are common but risky because they reduce accountability. We introduce stronger controls and secure sharing so teams can access what they need without exposing the actual passwords, and so you can see who has access to what.

slots.label: Question 4
slots.default: Will this slow down our team’s access?

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: No, done well, it speeds things up. A password manager fills credentials automatically, so staff spend less time resetting forgotten passwords. Our aim is security that improves usability rather than getting in the way of everyday work.

slots.label: Question 5
slots.default: Is this a one-off project or ongoing?

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: We can introduce secure password management as a project, then provide ongoing reviews, password policy, user access management and multi-factor authentication reviews, so account security keeps pace as your business, team and cloud applications change.
